correctness.rationale: For bounded-degree grids, Hanf locality reduces any fixed-rank sentence to truncated rooted-ball counts. For every full-plane or half-plane rooted type, disjoint replicated placements yield linearly many independent positive-probability trials and high-probability saturation; every remaining type occurs only in four fixed corner patches. Hence the limiting event is a function of finitely many independent Bernoulli colours and its probability is an integer polynomial in fixed p. Uniqueness of corner diagonal vertices follows from the unique maximum of binomial(2j,a) shortest-path counts at a=j; bounded j makes this FO definable. Four independent t-bit corner codes have S4-orbit sizes 1,4,6,12,24 with stated counts. A gap-free subset-sum lemma proves every count 0..a^4 is attainable for a>=4. Finite checker tests orbit counts and path maximizers; infinity is established by proofs, not enumeration.

value.rationale: A nontrivial zero-one failure from finite boundary corners is promoted to a complete first-order probability-spectrum classification: every limit is dyadic and every dyadic is eventually exactly realizable using formulas in an unoriented single-edge graph language. The result makes a structural bulk/boundary distinction for random unary expansions of natural finite product-of-chain cover graphs and gives a complete endpoint rather than isolated example or computation.
